entries.review_note: Chabashira's Icarus comparison is an undated internal metaphor; anonymous boy not identified.
She describes her own gamble and distress; no external confirmation of the boy's supposed wrath.
Yamauchi assessment is a printed visual dossier, not an observed demonstration.
Students are told this is a luxury trip, so the exam cannot be preloaded into their shipboard knowledge.
Class A insults and shoves; Sudō restrains from starting a fight, motivation unspecified.
Hirata leaves to help another peer; alleged relationship trouble with Karuizawa is hearsay.
Ike and Kushida exchange permission to use first names, not a confirmed romance.
Island's dimensions and full ship circuit are noted; future use of geography remains undisclosed.
Phones and belongings are surrendered; Horikita's shivering is seen but cause unconfirmed.
Chabashira calls roll for D and Mashima of A leads the public briefing.
Mashima announces the surprise island test, with no evidence of prior student knowledge.
Tents, lights, matches and individual hygiene provisions are allocated by the school.
Freedom is the named theme but purchases consume special-test points, not S-System balances.
Mashima says remaining island-test points are added to class points after the examination.
Class A's absent student produces a reported 30-point reduction to 270.
Mandatory tracking watches and removal warning are stated as school policy.
Temperature, pulse, GPS and emergency alert are listed as watch capabilities, not measured reliability.
The written 30-point health-retirement rule is nonreversible and class-scoped.
Environmental pollution costs 20; one missed 8 AM or 8 PM roll call costs 5 per student.
Disqualifying interclass violence/theft also forfeits the offender's private points.
Test balance bottoms at zero, but this does not negate instant-disqualification rules.
Registered camp remains the roll-call site; moving requires suitable justification.
Portable cardboard toilet and enclosure are supplied; Shinohara's disapproval is personal.
Ike-Shinohara conflict concerns privacy and point expenditure, not a fixed universal trait.
Hoshinomiya greets Chabashira and hints at their past, the details unproven here.
An occupied special site expires after eight hours; its bonus point cannot be spent during exam.
Leader-specific card is required to register spots; using another class's occupied site costs 50.
Correct and wrong leader guesses have distinct fifty-point outcomes; exposure wipes occupancy bonus.
Class leader selection is required by first roll call, with a school fallback and qualified replacement.
Horikita acknowledges practical wilderness contributions by Ike and Sudō despite prior disdain.
Hirata advocates one paid toilet after debate; this is an observed contingent coalition choice.
Kushida volunteers for exploration and reluctant classmates follow; group motivation cannot be perfectly isolated.
Kōenji asks what others see but conceals his precise observation and then leaves.
Kiyotaka and Sakura find Class A's cave and witness card handling while hidden.
Katsuragi, overheard by Kiyotaka, explains his route inference from a path seen on the ship; case ownership belongs to Katsuragi.
Ike and associates locate a river and possible camp; water quality is not proven by the find.
Kushida nominates Horikita and Hirata obtains her assigned card; an initially secret role is set.
Ike drinks from the river after a dare; one drink does not verify ongoing drinking-water safety.
Sudō proposes boiling water while defusing argument; implementation and water safety remain separate.
Girls initially take both tents, prompting a temporary shelter dispute, not a durable camp constitution.
